Rationale.CS1_Results_vs_Conclusion: All evaluable conclusions in the documentation match the results originally recorded in the code implementation notebooks. Tournament Elo ratings in Table 1 exactly match values computed in tournament_results.ipynb. Puzzle-solving analysis in puzzle_results.ipynb confirms 'final cumulative solve rate exceeds the last layer's rate' (93.0% vs 88.6%). The forgotten puzzle example (Puzzle 58Ib0: Rxg7+ vs Kf1) in forgotten_puzzle_figure.ipynb matches Figure 4 description. Policy dynamics metrics in policy_metrics.ipynb confirm the three-phase pattern. The replication study verified Kendall τ changes: early (+0.31), middle (+0.09), late (+0.76).
Rationale.CS2_Plan_vs_Implementation: A plan file exists (plan.md) and all steps in the final version are reflected in the implementation. Methodology: (1) Logit lens extension implemented in leela_logit_lens.py with zero ablation method; (2) T82-768x15x24h model (lc0-original.onnx) used throughout; (3) Tournament evaluation in scripts/tournament.py and tournament_results.ipynb; (4) Puzzle evaluation in scripts/evaluate_puzzles.py and puzzle_results.ipynb; (5) Policy dynamics in policy_metrics.ipynb; (6) Concept preferences in scripts/evaluate_concepts.py. All six planned experiments (tournament, Lichess, puzzles, forgetting, policy dynamics, concepts) have corresponding implementations.
Rationale.CS3_Effect_Size: Reported effects have clearly non-trivial magnitude relative to baseline: (1) Tournament Elo: 1820 point improvement from Input (443) to Full model (2263), with phase differences of +564 (early), +50 (middle), +1206 (late); (2) Puzzle solving: 4.4% gap between cumulative (93.0%) and final layer (88.6%) rates; (3) Kendall τ: late phase change (0.76) is 8x the middle phase change (0.09); (4) JS divergence drops ~50% from early (0.773) to late (0.380). These differences are orders of magnitude larger than measurement noise.
Rationale.CS4_Justification: All key design choices and intermediate conclusions are explicitly justified: (1) Logit lens methodology justified via mathematical derivation in Appendix B with reference to prior work; (2) Three-phase boundaries (L5, L10, L11) empirically derived from tournament progression data; (3) Concept preference analysis follows McGrath et al. (2022) with explicit formula Δcℓ = Eπℓ[Δcm]; (4) Forgotten puzzles conclusion supported by quantitative gap (4.4%), specific example with probability trajectories, and value head validation; (5) Safety prior hypothesis explicitly stated as correlational with supporting concept preference data. No unjustified leaps in reasoning identified.
Rationale.CS5_Statistical_Significance: Key experimental results report appropriate measures of uncertainty: (1) Policy distribution metrics (Figures 6-7): median with 25-75th and 5-95th percentile ranges clearly explained; (2) Concept preferences (Figure 5): 95% confidence intervals explicitly reported; (3) Tournament results: BayesElo methodology cited (Coulom 2008); (4) Puzzle results: sample sizes reported (n=851-1642 per Elo range, 10,000 total); (5) Results shown across multiple conditions (τ=0 vs τ=1, multiple time controls) provide robustness. The methodology for uncertainty estimation is clearly explained where provided.
